title: Operational Hardening and Safe Migration Playbook for Private Deploys
author: Emma Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes an engineering-first process for operational hardening and safe workload migration for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem bundles). It combines pre-migration verification, staged rollout guidance, continuous telemetry checks, and a deterministic rollback matrix to minimize customer downtime and data risk during model, runtime, or infra migrations.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Private deployments delivered via Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem) including model swaps, runtime upgrades, kernel/quantization changes, and capacity migration between pools.
- Audience: Field engineers, SREs, deployment engineers, solutions architects, and customer success leads supporting private customers.

Owner and escalation:
- Primary owner: Private Deployments Team (eng-private-deployments).
- Runbook owner: Emma Chen (Runbook maintainer).
- On-call escalation: Private-deploys oncall -> Eng SRE -> Platform Lead.

Success criteria and SLOs for migration activity:
- Migration must not exceed 2x historical 1h error rate at 95th percentile for production traffic during the 30-minute canary window.
- Mean token latency must not regress by more than 15% from baseline across 99th percentile after steady-state (1 hour).
- No data-loss incidents (0 lost requests) and KV/embedding cache semantics preserved.

Prerequisites checklist (must be green before starting):
| Item | Description | Owner | Required state |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer readiness call | Confirm maintenance window and rollback authority | Solutions Eng | scheduled/acknowledged |
| Backups | Snapshot model artifacts, KV cache snapshot if stateful | Field Engineer | completed |
| Telemetry hooks | Ensure sampling rules and traces are enabled at 100% for canary nodes | SRE | enabled |
| Capacity reserve | 20% spare GPU headroom in same region or burst pool | Capacity Planner | verified |
| Access | Field engineer has customer admin KMS & SSH keys (if onprem) | Field Engineer | verified |

Pre-migration validation (pre-flight):
1) Inventory and compatibility matrix
- Validate model binary ABI, quantization profile, and kernel compatibility against runtime version using the compatibility-checker tool:
  - CLI: rdx-compat-check --model <MODEL_PATH> --runtime <RUNTIME_TAG> --output summary.json
  - Expected exit 0. Attach summary.json to migration ticket.
2) Smoke harness in staging mirror
- Deploy identical staging shard with 10% representative KV sizes, and run the canonical smoke set (prompt-shard-smoke.json) for 30 minutes.
3) Telemetry assertion baseline
- Collect 1h of baseline telemetry (latency percentiles, error rates, token generation rate) and store in migration-buffer: bucket://redwood-migrations/<customer>/<migration-id>/baseline.json

Staged rollout plan (recommended):
- Phase 0: Dry-run verify (no traffic) — deploy to a single node in the staging cluster and run smoke tests (20–30 minutes).
- Phase 1: Canary (1–3% traffic) — route a small percentage of production traffic to new runtime/model variant for 30 minutes. Use runtime routing policy: ROUTE_POLICY=migration-canary-<id>.
- Phase 2: Ramp (5–25%) — 4 sequential ramps (5, 10, 15, 25%) each with a 15–30 minute observation window.
- Phase 3: Partial production (50%) — if all metrics stable, move to 50% for 30–60 minutes with full end-to-end smoke across customer flows.
- Phase 4: Full cutover (100%) — proceed only after green across all checks for at least 1 hour.

Metric checks and automated abort criteria (each check evaluated continuously during windows):
- Error rate (5xx) must not exceed baseline*2 for canary window or baseline + 1% absolute for larger ramps.
- Latency: P99 token latency regression >15% triggers abort.
- Quality guardrails: Automated evals on canonical prompts must not drop top-1 semantic score by >6 points (or configured customer threshold).
- Resource saturation: GPU memory usage >90% or CPU steal >40% triggers abort and immediate rollback.
- Request failure modes: Increase in KV cache misses >2x baseline -> investigate, hold ramp.

Rollback matrix (deterministic mapping of failure mode -> rollback action):
- Failure: P99 latency regression >15% during any window -> Action: Immediate route revert to prior variant, scale new nodes to 0, alert SRE and field engineer.
- Failure: Error rate >2x baseline in canary -> Action: Pause routing, scale down canary nodes, run 'rdx-dump-logs' and gather stack traces.
- Failure: Quality regression detected on canonical evals -> Action: Stop ramp, close canary, replace candidate model with previous build; if quick fix unavailable, rollback.
- Failure: KMS access error for decryption of model weights -> Action: Revoke new deployment, rollback and coordinate with security/KMS owner.

Immediate rollback commands (examples):
- API rollback (hosted control plane cooperating with private control plane):
  - curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' \n    https://private-control.<customer>.redwood/api/v1/rollouts/<migration-id>/rollback
- On-prem operator (kubectl example):
  - kubectl -n redwood set image deploy/runtime runtime=redwood/runtime:<previous-tag> --record
  - kubectl rollout status deploy/runtime -n redwood --timeout=10m

Post-rollback triage checklist:
1) Capture telemetry from rollback window and retain for 30 days in migration bucket.
2) Open a detailed incident record with root cause hypothesis within 24 hours.
3) Schedule a fix/patch release or adjust config and re-run a scheduled test migration in staging.

Day-2 operational hardening tasks (post-cutover):
- Config hardening: Enforce CIS-like kernel tuning for onprem images (sysctl settings) — include the sample sysctl block below in the node bootstrap:
  - net.core.somaxconn=1024
  - vm.swappiness=10
  - vm.dirty_ratio=15
- Token sampling & traces: Maintain 10% request trace sampling for first 72 hours, then drop to customer agreed sampling (default 1%).
- Log retention: Increase debug-level retention for migration nodes to 168 hours (7 days) and route to customer-owned S3 for audit.

Telemetry and acceptance checks (post-cutover steady-state):
- Validation run (24h): Run full acceptance harness that includes throughput, latency, and guardrail checks.
- Customer smoke test: Coordinate with customer success to validate critical flows using the customer acceptance test suite.
- Drift detection: Run nightly compare of embedding distribution, per-prompt generation length, and tokenization diffs for first 72 hours.

Packaging and artifact concerns:
- Model artifact immutability: Tag artifacts with semantic version + digest (e.g., model-v1.4+sha256:abc123). The runtime only pulls artifacts that match digest.
- Image signing: All runtime images for production use must be signed with internal cosign keys. Verification command example: cosign verify --key /secure/keys/cosign.pub <image>.

Risk matrix (summary):
- High risk: Stateful cache mismatch, KMS decryption errors, embedded token loss during migration. Mitigation: snapshots, dry-run with representative KV sizes, pre-checks for KMS policies.
- Medium risk: Performance regressions due to kernel selection or quantization. Mitigation: compat-checker, small density canaries, telemetry thresholds.
- Low risk: Observability gaps; mitigated by pre-enabling traces and temporary elevated sampling.

Operational play examples (snippets):
- Sample alert policy (Pseudo):
  - alert: Migration_P99_Latency_Regression
    expr: (migration_p99_latency / baseline_p99_latency) > 1.15
    for: 5m
    labels: { severity: page }

- Minimal acceptance smoke curl test:
  - curl -X POST https://private-api.customer.example/v1/generate \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"<candidate>","prompt":"Hello world","max_tokens":16}'

Related pages and artifacts to attach before starting:
- Link: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/private-deploy-onboarding-and-failover-runbook-2026 (onboarding checklist)
- Link: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/post-installation-telemetry-and-acceptance-checklist-2026 (telemetry norms)
- Artifact: compatibility-checker summary.json

Post-mortem and continuous improvement:
- After any migration that required rollback or exceeded thresholds, run a 72-hour retrospective including: timeline, telemetry snapshots, root cause, corrective actions, and a retro ticket with owner and target fix date.

Appendix A — Quick reference commands:
- rdx-compat-check --model /artifacts/model.tar.gz --runtime runtime:2026-02-01 --output /tmp/compat.json
- rdx-deploy --bundle /artifacts/private-bundle.tar.gz --target canary-node --annotations migration-id=<id>
- rdx-metrics tail --window 30m --filter migration=<id>

Appendix B — Minimal staging smoke suite (file: prompt-shard-smoke.json)
- [
  { "prompt": "Summarize the following text in one sentence:" },
  { "prompt": "Extract the product name from: 'Order 9382: Redwood Tuner'" },
  { "prompt": "Rewrite for clarity: 'Received bad kernel selection leading to slow tokens'" }
]
